correctness.rationale: A geometric fixed point has an H-invariant minimal simplex of disjoint blocks. Transitivity forces full support and one orbit of blocks, hence a unique barycenter. Invariant partitions are precisely block systems and correspond to H_x<=K<=H, proving discreteness and the subgroup-count formula, including regular cyclic and conjugation actions. For full Young factors of size at least two, the only admissible vertex orbits consist of whole-macroblock unions and singleton orbits; compatible supports yield the twin-singleton complex L_t. Duplicating a singleton joins a cone on its link, whose inclusion is nullhomotopic via the original vertex; iterated Mayer–Vietoris and Gottstein’s integral homology of ordinary D([m]) yield the complete torsion-free ranks.
risks: The Young classification requires full symmetric factors and no singleton macroblocks.
Homology splitting is abelian and not claimed as a canonical external symmetry-module splitting.
